meta.title: Freefall Simulator
meta.description: See how body position changes a skydiver's flight in freefall.

freefall.intro: Turn the positions below on and off and watch what happens to the skydiver. The dots are the air rushing past you: the faster they rise, the faster you fall.
freefall.sceneLabel: Animation of a skydiver in freefall, belly to earth, seen from the side.

explain.neutral: Neutral box position: hips down, arms and legs symmetrical. The air pushes evenly on your body, so you fall stable without moving.
explain.legsStretch: Legs stretched: the air pushes your legs up, your head drops and you move forward.
explain.legsTuck: Legs tucked: your legs leave the airflow, your back tilts and you slide backward.
explain.armsForward: Arms forward: the air pushes the front of your body up and you slide backward.
explain.armsBack: Arms pulled back: the front of your body catches less air, your head drops and you move forward.
explain.archMore: More arch: your body is more stable and has less drag, so you fall faster.
explain.archFlat: No arch: more area against the air, so you fall slower, but you are less stable and may rock.
explain.dipLeft: Left shoulder down: air spills off your left side and you turn left.
explain.dipRight: Right shoulder down: air spills off your right side and you turn right.

freefall.disclaimer: This animation is a learning aid to help you understand how freefall works. Trust your instructor, and always take your questions to a certified instructor.

combos.moreArea: Result: more of your body is exposed to the wind, which slows your fall a little. To slow down more, you can also reduce your arch (de-arch).
combos.slowFall: This position is used to slow your fall rate. You can also turn your face to the side, which slows the fall rate a little more.

motionNote.text: The animation is paused because your system asks for less motion on screen.
